user.title: Add a TV running Webmote
user.description: The address and port shown on Webmote's screen on the TV, like 192.168.1.20 and 8080. TVs on the same network are usually found by themselves.

data_description.host: The TV's IP address (Webmote refuses names).

zeroconf_confirm.title: Add {name}?
zeroconf_confirm.description: {name} runs Webmote. Next, it shows a six-digit PIN in a corner of the screen.

pair.title: Pair with {name}
pair.description: Type the PIN now shown in a corner of the TV's screen (it's also on Webmote's own screen on the TV).

reauth_confirm.title: Pair with {name} again
reauth_confirm.description: {name} no longer knows Home Assistant: someone pressed New PIN on the TV, or 20 newer devices paired. Next, it shows a new PIN.

error.cannot_connect: Can't reach the TV. Check that it's on, on this network, and that Webmote's remote service is on (TV settings, Accessibility).
error.not_an_address: Type the TV's IP address, like 192.168.1.20.
error.too_many_tries: Too many tries. Wait {wait} seconds, then try again.
error.unknown: The TV gave an unexpected answer.

abort.not_supported: This Webmote is too old to add by itself: update it to 0.4.0 or newer.
abort.update_webmote: Update Webmote on the TV to 0.4.0 or newer, then add it again.
abort.wrong_device: That's a different TV from the one being paired again.
